Let \(x\) be the mass of NaHCO₃ and \(y\) be the mass of MgCO₃, with \(x+y=15.00\).

Molar masses:
- NaHCO₃ = 84.006 g/mol
- Na₂CO₃ = 105.988 g/mol
- MgCO₃ = 84.313 g/mol
- MgO = 40.304 g/mol

Residue from NaHCO₃:
\[
2\text{NaHCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3
\]
so residue factor:
\[
\frac{105.988}{2(84.006)} = 0.63084
\]

Residue from MgCO₃:
\[
\text{MgCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{MgO}
\]
so residue factor:
\[
\frac{40.304}{84.313} = 0.47803
\]

Thus:
\[
0.63084x + 0.47803(15.00-x) = 8.80
\]
\[
0.15281x = 1.6296
\]
\[
x = 10.664 \text{ g}
\]

Mass percentage of NaHCO₃:
\[
\frac{10.664}{15.00} \times 100 = 71.1\%
\]

ANSWER: 71.1
